content: 1. Avoid or consider using an alternative drug when co-administering perampanel with pyrazinamide and pexidartinib, as both agents increase inhibition of gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of these drugs. Increased perampanel dosage may be required. 2. Pexidartinib can cause hepatotoxicity. Avoid or use an alternative drug when co-administering pexidartinib with rifampin, as both increase inhibition of gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of these drugs. 3. Rifampin increases the level or effect of pexidartinib by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the pexidartinib dose as per the drug monograph dosage modifications. After discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor for three elimination half-lives, the previous pexidartinib dose may be resumed. 4. Rifampin decreases the level or effect of pirtobrutinib by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 5. Pyrazinamide and pretomanid increase each other's toxicity. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Pretomanid regimens are associated with hepatotoxicity. Avoid alcohol and hepatotoxic agents, including herbal supplements and drugs other than bedaquiline and linezolid. 6. Rifampin increases the toxicity of pitavastatin through mechanisms involving other pathways (see comment). Avoid or use an alternative drug. OATP1B1 inhibitors may increase the risk of myopathy. 7. Rifampin decreases the levels of pomalidomide by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism, hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism, and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 8. Rifampin decreases the level or effect of ponatinib by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug unless the benefits of co-administration outweigh the risks of ponatinib underexposure. Monitor for signs of reduced efficacy. 9. Rifampin decreases the level or effect of ponesimod by mechanisms involving other pathways (see comment). Avoid or use an alternative drug. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 and UGT1A1 inducers (e.g., rifampin, phenytoin, carbamazepine) may decrease systemic exposure to ponesimod. The clinical relevance of this interaction is unclear. 10. Rifampin decreases the level or effect of pralsetinib by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, double the current pralsetinib dose starting on Day 7 of co-administration with a strong CYP3A inducer. After the inducer has been discontinued for at least 14 days, resume the previous pralsetinib dose. 11. Rifampin decreases the level or effect of prednisolone and prednisone by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 12. Rifampin decreases the level or effect of pretomanid by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Pretomanid regimens are associated with hepatotoxicity. Avoid alcohol and hepatotoxic agents, including herbal supplements and drugs other than bedaquiline and linezolid. 13. Rifampin decreases the level or effect of primaquine by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 14. Rifampin decreases the level or effect of progesterone intravaginal gel, micronized progesterone, and natural progesterone by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Use of nonhormonal contraceptives is advised. 15. Rifampin decreases the level or effect of propofol by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2B6 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 16. Rifampin and pyrazinamide increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism, leading to additive hepatotoxicity. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 17. Rifampin decreases the level or effect of quazepam, quetiapine, quinidine, quizartinib, ranolazine, and repaglinide by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 18. Rifampin decreases the level or effect of repotrectinib by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 19. Rifampin increases the level or effect of resmetirom through mechanisms involving other pathways (see comment). Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid co-administration of resmetirom (an OATP1B1/3 substrate) with OATP1B1/3 inhibitors. 20. Rifampin increases levels of revefenacin by mechanisms involving other pathways (see comment). Avoid or use an alternative drug. OATP1B1 and OATP1B3 transport inhibitors may increase systemic exposure to revefenacin's active metabolite. Co-administration is not recommended. 21. Rifampin decreases the level or effect of ribociclib by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Co-administration of ribociclib with strong CYP3A inducers should be avoided. 22. Rifampin decreases the level or effect of rifabutin by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 23. Rifampin decreases the level or effect of rimegepant by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 24. Rifampin decreases levels of abiraterone by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Avoid co-administration of abiraterone with strong CYP3A4 inducers. If a strong CYP3A4 inducer must be used, increase abiraterone dosage frequency from once daily to twice daily. 25. Rifampin decreases the level or effect of alfentanil, alfuzosin, and alosetron by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the level or effect of rifampin through other mechanisms (see comment). Use caution and monitor closely. Concomitant antacid administration may reduce rifampin absorption. Daily doses of rifampin should be given at least 1 hour before ingestion of antacids. 27. Rifampin decreases the level or effect of ambrisentan by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration was associated with a transient two-fold increase in ambrisentan AUC; however, by Day 7, rifampin had no clinically important effect on ambrisentan. 28. Rifampin decreases the level or effect of amikacin by P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Rifampin decreases the level or effect of amitriptyline by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Rifampin decreases the level or effect of amlodipine by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Rifampin decreases levels of amobarbital by increasing metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Rifampin decreases the level or effect of antipyrine by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Apalutamide decreases the level or effect of rifampin by increasing elimination. Use caution and monitor closely. Apalutamide weakly induces OATP1B1 and may decrease systemic exposure of drugs that are OATP1B1 substrates. 34. Rifampin decreases the level or effect of armodafinil by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Rifampin decreases the level or effect of artesunate by increasing metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration may decrease AUC and peak plasma concentration of active artesunate metabolite (DHA) by inducing UGT. Monitor for decreased efficacy. 36. Rifampin decreases the level or effect of asenapine by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Rifampin decreases the level or effect of atogepant by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Recommended dosage of atogepant (an OATP1B1 substrate) with concomitant use of OATP inhibitors is 10 mg or 30 mg once daily. 38. Rifampin decreases the level or effect of atorvastatin by P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Rifampin decreases levels of atovaquone by increasing metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Rifampin decreases the level or effect of avanafil by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. For patients with erectile dysfunction, monitor response carefully due to potential for decreased effectiveness. 41. Rifampin decreases the level or effect of avatrombopag by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. When treating ITP, co-administration of avatrombopag with a moderate or strong dual CYP2C9/3A4 inducer requires an increased avatrombopag starting dose. Refer to the drug monograph for specific recommendations. 42. Azithromycin increases the level or effect of rifampin by P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Rifampin decreases the level or effect of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Rifampin decreases the level or effect of belumosudil by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Increase belumosudil dosage to 200 mg orally twice daily when co-administered with strong CYP3A inducers. 45. Rifampin decreases levels of bendamustine by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Concentrations of active metabolites may be increased. 46. Rifampin decreases the level or effect of benzhydrocodone/acetaminophen by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Caution when discontinuing CYP3A4 inducers co-administered with benzhydrocodone (a prodrug of hydrocodone); plasma concentrations of hydrocodone may increase, potentially resulting in fatal respiratory depression. 47. Rifampin decreases levels of berotralstat by P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Berotralstat increases the level or effect of rifampin by P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Monitor or titrate P-gp substrate dose if co-administered. 48. Rifampin decreases the level or effect of bexagliflozin by other mechanisms (see comment). Modify therapy or monitor closely. Bexagliflozin is a major substrate of UGT1A9. If co-administered with a UGT1A9 inducer, consider adding another antihyperglycemic agent in patients requiring additional glycemic control. 49. Rifampin decreases the level or effect of bexarotene by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 50. Rifampin decreases the level or effect of bortezomib by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 51. Rifampin decreases the level or effect of bosentan by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 52. Bosutinib increases levels of rifampin by P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 53. Rifampin decreases levels of brentuximab vedotin by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 54. Rifampin decreases the level or effect of brexpiprazole by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Double brexpiprazole dose over 1–2 weeks if administered with a strong CYP3A4 inducer. 55. Rifampin decreases the level or effect of brivaracetam by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. The dose of brivaracetam should be increased up to 100% (i.e., double the dosage) in patients while receiving concomitant treatment with rifampin. 56. Rifampin decreases the level or effect of bromocriptine by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 57. Rifampin decreases the level or effect of budesonide by P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 58. Rifampin decreases the level or effect of buprenorphine by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely.
